h1: Taksila Hotel Maha Sarakham — the central 4-star the locals keep recommending
intro: Ask anyone in Maha Sarakham for a city hotel they trust, and Taksila Hotel usually comes up near the top of the list · It's a 4-star property on Somthawilrad Road in the Talat (market) district, right in the centre of town, an easy walk to restaurants and the night market · Open since 2000 and fully renovated in 2023 · 35 Thai-toned rooms with an outdoor pool, fitness centre, spa and free covered parking · Guests most often praise the spacious, clean rooms, friendly staff and a buffet breakfast that punches above the room rate · from approx. ฿900/night

body.html: Taksila Hotel is one of those properties that has been part of Maha Sarakham for a long time · It has operated since 2000 and went through a full renovation in 2023, which freshened up the rooms and common areas · The hotel sits on Somthawilrad Road in the Talat (market) district, right in the city centre — a location that puts food and the night market just a few minutes' walk away · The décor leans into wood tones and Thai detailing, with carved woodwork that several guests single out as giving the place a local character you don't get from a typical chain.

Rooms range from Grand Deluxe and Junior Suite up to the Grand Suite · The thing guests agree on most is that the rooms are spacious and clean, with comfortable beds · Many reviews praise the strong water pressure and plentiful hot water — a small detail a lot of provincial hotels get wrong · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, minibar, satellite TV, a work desk, kettle and safe · The honest downside: some bathroom construction looks dated and a touch rough in places, a few rooms have low bathroom doorways, and the walls between rooms aren't especially thick — you may hear your neighbours on a quiet night.
"Huge, clean room, comfy bed, strong hot water, lovely staff and big covered parking. The breakfast was better than the price deserved — the best-value hotel I've stayed at in Maha Sarakham."

For a city hotel of this size the common facilities are well covered · There's an outdoor pool with a separate children's pool, which makes it a comfortable pick for families · You also get a fitness centre, a spa and an in-house restaurant · The thing guests rave about most is the buffet breakfast, which feels generous for the room price, with savoury and sweet dishes plus local options · A few reviewers note the spread isn't as varied as big-city hotels — no fresh juice or cereal, for example — but it's solid value at this rate · Drivers especially love the large, free, covered car park.

Location is the main draw here · The hotel sits in the heart of Maha Sarakham's market district, within walking distance of food stalls and the night market · It's close to government offices, the hospital and Rajabhat Maha Sarakham University, while the main Mahasarakham University campus in Kham Riang is about a 20-minute drive · That makes it a natural choice for people coming for official business, parents visiting students during graduation season, and travellers who want to stay central and walk · It scores 8.5 from 26 reviews on Trip.com and ranks among the top hotels in Maha Sarakham on TripAdvisor, which reflects broadly happy guests.

To be straight about it, Taksila Hotel suits travellers who want a dependable city hotel — spacious rooms, good service and a central spot at a price that's easy on the wallet · It isn't a design boutique or a luxury resort, but it delivers the essentials and does them well for the money · The trade-off you have to accept is the ageing building — some dated bathroom finishes, thin walls, and a few reviews noting that housekeeping standards aren't perfectly consistent visit to visit · Even so, against other options in town at the same price, it remains the name locals recommend most often.

A tip from reading the reviews: if you're coming during a university graduation period in Maha Sarakham, rooms sell out fast and rates climb, so book several weeks ahead · For a quieter night, ask for a room away from the road and not adjoining a busy room, since the walls aren't thick · Families should consider the larger suites — only a small price step up — and kids will enjoy the children's pool beside the main one · For dinner, walk out into the market district, which is full of good local spots, rather than eating in-house every meal.

honestSummary: Taksila Hotel is a city hotel that sells dependability, spacious rooms, good service and a central location at an easy price — with a pool, free parking and a great-value breakfast, it suits both business visitors and families coming to see students · The trade-off is an ageing building, some dated bathroom finishes and thin walls.

faq.q: Where is Taksila Hotel Maha Sarakham and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's at 1227/68 Somthawilrad Road, Talat, Mueang Maha Sarakham, right in the central market district · You can walk to restaurants and the night market · It's close to Rajabhat Maha Sarakham University, Maha Sarakham Hospital and Wat Mahachai (about 5 minutes by car) · The main Mahasarakham University campus in Kham Riang is about a 20-minute drive · Free covered parking is available.

faq.q: How much does Taksila Hotel cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿900/night for a Grand Deluxe room · Junior Suites start near ฿1,300, and the largest Grand Suite is around ฿1,800 · Prices vary by season and package — especially during graduation periods, when rates rise — so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Taksila Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both · There's an outdoor pool with a separate children's pool, plus a fitness centre and spa on site · Parking is a large, free, covered car park, which is a detail self-drivers frequently praise.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are decorated in Thai wood tones · Most guests praise them as spacious and clean, with comfortable beds and strong hot water · Each room has air conditioning, a fridge, minibar, satellite TV and a safe · The downsides noted are some dated bathroom finishes, thin walls, and a few reviews saying housekeeping standards aren't perfectly consistent every visit.

faq.q: Is the breakfast at Taksila Hotel any good, and is it included?
faq.a: The buffet breakfast is praised as great value for the room price, with savoury, sweet and local dishes · Some reviews note the variety isn't as wide as big-city hotels — no fresh juice or cereal, for instance · It's included in some rates, so check when you book.

faq.q: Who is Taksila Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a dependable city hotel — spacious rooms, good service and a central spot at an easy price · That includes business visitors, parents visiting students or attending graduation, and families who want to stay central and walk · It's the name locals in Maha Sarakham recommend most often.
